title: Composite golden-set watchdog for canary flips with weighted shadowing
creator: Ava Patel
description: Problem: Current canary gating relies on individual metric thresholds evaluated independently (e.g., perplexity, toxicity, token-regen rate). This leads to noisy decisions during low traffic canaries and misses multi-metric regressions that are subtle but impactful. Goal: Implement a composite golden-set watchdog that evaluates candidate model versions against curated golden prompt sets (global + per-customer subsets) using an ensemble scoring strategy, confidence estimation, and dynamic traffic weighting. The watchdog will integrate with canary/A-B controllers and the shadow routing layer to enable safer flips and automatic rollbacks when composite score regressions exceed calibrated bounds.
acceptance_criteria: A composite eval score is computed per rollout using a weighted aggregation of at least three signal classes: primary correctness metrics (scorecards), safety regressions (toxicity/filters), and latency/regression heuristics (token-regen, truncation).
Per-customer golden subsets can be bound to a rollout such that the composite score considers the top-10 highest-risk customers first for sensitivity tuning.

Confidence intervals (bootstrap or Bayesian) are reported for composite scores; rollouts only flip automatically when the upper bound of candidate-model delta is below the negative threshold (improvement) or above the positive threshold (regression) for N consecutive evaluation windows.
Shadow traffic path can be enabled with configurable weight and does not affect user-visible latency; shadow results feed the watchdog without affecting production routing.
Automatic rollback triggers an orchestration action in the rollout controller and creates a detailed incident in the Console with implicated prompts and example outputs.
UI: Console shows composite scorecard, per-signal breakdown, confidence interval, and a timeline of decisions for each canary/A-B experiment.
End-to-end tests (unit + integration + e2e) verify composite scoring, thresholding logic, and that rollback API is called under simulated regressions.
Performance: eval scoring for a canary with 2k golden prompts completes within target evaluation window (<= 45s) when run on the eval cluster used by rollouts.
rollout_plan: Design phase (this ticket): finalize composite metric definitions, per-customer weighting model, and watchdog API contract.
Implementation phase: implement scorer service changes, add confidence estimation module, expose watchdog endpoints to rollout controller and shadow router.
Staging test: run synthetic canaries (with injected regressions) using shadow traffic, validate rollback latency and alerting.
Beta: enable for internal tenants and a small set of opt-in customers; collect live false-positive/false-negative rates and tune thresholds.
GA: flip on by default for new runtime releases with observable default thresholds and an opt-out for customers.
Post-GA: telemetry-backed threshold tuning and ML-based weighting suggestion in Redwood Optimize.
monitoring: Alerts: P0 PagerDuty alert if composite_delta > configured_regression_threshold AND composite_ci_lower > 0 for 3 consecutive windows
Slack: summary digest to #rollouts when a canary passes/fails with top-5 offending prompts linked
Audit log: record all auto-rollback decisions with payload (model_version, traffic_weights, composite_score_breakdown) to customer audit store when rollout is private/dedicated.
SLO: ensure watchdog evaluation latency 95th percentile <= 45s for up to 2k golden prompts.
testing: Unit: scorer weight math, CI estimation, null-handling, and per-customer subset selection.
Integration: scorer service <-> rollout controller handshake, rollback API invocation, shadow router event stream.
E2E: synthetic canary that injects a controlled safety regression and verifies rollback triggers and incident creation.
Load: run 5 concurrent canaries with 2k prompts each on eval cluster to validate compute and queueing behavior.
A/B experiments: compare binary rollback policy vs. composite-watchdog-driven policies over 4 weeks on internal traffic.
notes: Metric composition: propose starting weights: correctness 0.6, safety 0.25, latency/regression 0.15. These will be tunable per-project and learnable over time.
Confidence estimation: prefer bootstrap resampling for initial rollout (simplicity) with plan to evaluate Bayesian hierarchical models later.
Per-customer sensitivity: customers with SLAs get stricter thresholds and prioritized prompt subsets; ensure data residency rules are followed for private deployments.
Edge case: low-sample canaries should defer to conservative behavior (no-auto-flip) and flag for manual review.
Fallback: if watcher service becomes unavailable, rollout controller should move to safe-mode (no automatic flips) and alert ops.
